text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Electricity prices are expected to fall next year.

- The opposition in parliament is not satisfied with Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen's statements on his share option sale in 1987. Politicians demand an explanation in writing by the embattled minister.
- The government will increase minke whale catch quotas next year and may pave the way for exporting the meat.
- Norwegian school children are bad at mathematics and way below the average among students in 39 countries, a study shows.
- Today Aker shareholders will decide whether the offshore engineer group will merge with Kjell Inge Roekke's investment group RGI.
- A last-minute offer by the Finance Ministry clears the tax issue for Kjell Inge Roekke in the planned merger between his RGI investment group and Aker offshore group.
- Scandinavian Airlines System is cutting costs at the last moment after reporting a free fall in profits.
- Yesterday Kjell Inge Roekke and his RGI investment group landed a deal with Orkla under which Norway Seafoods gains control over the Frionor frozen food company.
- This year is a record year for car leasing in Norway.
- Union representatives at Hydro Aluminium support the plans by the management to cut staff.
